title: How many ways can a bracket make fourteen?
description: The book shows two times the bracket one plus six makes fourteen. The outside number and the bracket total are chosen from the pairs that multiply to fourteen, and then the total is split into two numbers.
teaching_notes: One idea: the outside number times the bracket total must be fourteen, so choose a pair of factors and then split the total. Watch for students who think the outside number must be two every time.

video_script.why: The child builds a bracket that makes a given number by choosing a pair of factors and splitting the total.
video_script.substitution: Choose a pair of numbers that multiply to the target, then split the second number into two numbers that add to it.
video_script.anchor: The target fourteen and the bracket form with an outside number and two numbers inside

final_answer.spoken: two times open bracket two plus five close bracket, two times open bracket three plus four close bracket, seven times open bracket one plus one close bracket and one times open bracket five plus nine close bracket

never_show: a bracket form that does not make fourteen
video_script.design: One idea: the outside number times the bracket total is fourteen. Uses the method of the solved example on a bracket. The target and the bracket form stay on the board all video.

beats.on_screen: a small title card From your book; the first way 2 × (1 + 6) = 14 and four empty bracket forms ____ × (____ + ____) = 14

marks.h1: the title card arrives: From your book
marks.h3: four empty bracket forms appear and glow

narration: <bookmark mark='h1'/>This is a question from your book about making fourteen.
<bookmark mark='h2'/>One way is two times open bracket one plus six close bracket.
<bookmark mark='h3'/>Can we find four other ways to get fourteen?

beats.on_screen: the example and the four empty forms stay on the board; Keeko sits at the corner of the board

marks.t1: Keeko sits at the corner of the board

narration: <bookmark mark='t1'/>Think and tell.

beats.on_screen: 2 × (1 + 6): the bracket total 7 is multiplied by the outside number 2 to give 14

marks.g1: the bracket 1 + 6 is circled and its total 7 appears
marks.g2: the outside number 2 multiplies the total 7

narration: <bookmark mark='g1'/>In the example, the numbers inside the bracket add to seven.
<bookmark mark='g2'/>The outside number two multiplies that total.
<bookmark mark='g3'/>We need an outside number and a total that give fourteen.

marks.gv1: the empty bracket form is written four times

narration: <bookmark mark='gv1'/>Given, an outside number and two numbers in a bracket, and the product is fourteen.

beats.on_screen: To find: four ways to fill the blanks

marks.fd1: the words four ways are written

narration: <bookmark mark='fd1'/>We have to find four ways to fill the blanks.

beats.on_screen: 14 = 1 × 14 and 14 = 2 × 7; the first number goes outside, the second is the bracket total

marks.s11: the pairs 1 and 14, and 2 and 7, are written
marks.s12: the first number is placed outside and the second inside

narration: <bookmark mark='s11'/>Step one, find pairs of numbers that multiply to fourteen.
One times fourteen is fourteen, and two times seven is fourteen.
<bookmark mark='s12'/>The first number goes outside the bracket, and the second is the total inside.

marks.s21: the outside number 2 and the total 7 are written
marks.s22: the splits 2 + 5 and 3 + 4 are written inside brackets

narration: <bookmark mark='s21'/>Step two, take two outside, so the bracket total must be seven.
<bookmark mark='s22'/>Two plus five is seven, and three plus four is seven.
That gives two ways.

marks.s31: the outside number 7 and the total 2 are written
marks.s32: the split 1 + 1 is written inside a bracket

narration: <bookmark mark='s31'/>Step three, take seven outside, so the bracket total must be two.
<bookmark mark='s32'/>One plus one is two, so seven times open bracket one plus one close bracket works.

marks.s41: the outside number 1 and the total 14 are written
marks.s42: the split 5 + 9 is written inside a bracket

narration: <bookmark mark='s41'/>Step four, take one outside, so the bracket total must be fourteen.
<bookmark mark='s42'/>Five plus nine is fourteen, so one times open bracket five plus nine close bracket works.

marks.s51: each bracket is worked out and its product meets 14

narration: <bookmark mark='s51'/>Step five, check each way by adding inside the bracket first.
<bookmark mark='s52'/>Two times seven is fourteen, for both of the first two.
Seven times two is fourteen, and one times fourteen is fourteen.

marks.a2: the first two ways are written in order
marks.a3: the last two ways are written in order

narration: <bookmark mark='a1'/>Four ways make fourteen.
<bookmark mark='a2'/>Two times open bracket two plus five close bracket. Two times open bracket three plus four close bracket.
<bookmark mark='a3'/>Seven times open bracket one plus one close bracket. One times open bracket five plus nine close bracket.
